Yes, all pre-1965 US quarters are made of 90% silver and 10% copper [d2][d3][d4]. Specifically, quarters struck by the U.S. Mint prior to 1965 were composed of 90% silver and 10% copper, a composition that was changed starting in 1965 when dimes and quarters began being minted in a copper-nickel clad composition with no silver content [d4][d1]. There is a minor caveat noted in one source: a handful of error coins were accidentally struck on silver planchets when they were intended to be clad, and there are some collector-only silver issues, but these are exceptions rather than the rule [d1]. In the United States, quarters minted in 1964 and earlier are 90% silver, making the pre-1965 date a reliable indicator of silver content [d5].
